shapeVolume: Original is an unmistakable quarter-annular conveyor with an outer coral arc, very short inner coral arc, radial blue-gray deck bands and four wooden supports under the curve.
All24-frame sheets show stable silhouette in each facing. S/E hide much of the support frame behind the outer rail; N/W expose a fairly flat orange support lip and very dark legs.

The target makes the rail and wood feel fuller and more crafted, with softly graded faces, a narrow warm edge highlight, readable joinery and restrained brass accents. Those are useful visible goals, not a mandate to copy its enlarged silhouette.
color: Source rails are muted salmon/coral with an abrupt face-value division. Deck is cool blue-gray; wooden lower faces are dark enough to read nearly black at small size.

Target coral/orange and honey wood have a warmer, richer but coherent palette. The approved native straight is more restrained than the target; its exact join palette must remain continuous on both ends.
lightingHighlights: Source rail tops read largely flat; the support under S/E carries a dark patch rather than warm readable volume.
Desired light is broad and soft, with enough top/side separation for rounded or softly faceted forms. No preferred horizontal key direction or ground shadow.
Target thin bright edge and strong gleam are aesthetic suggestions. Target image framing, halo pixels and high gloss are not required artifacts.
materialDetail: Target offers purposeful rail/deck structure, wood grain and joinery that can distinguish wood from deck without clutter.
The native family already has soft longitudinal rail highlights, blue-gray moving deck bands, honey wood and small brass fasteners. The corner should feel made by that same construction system.
Four legs, original polygon counts and exact source support construction are not aesthetic constraints.
readability: At55px and32px pitch the route and its turn remain legible. Fine source deck grooves merge into narrow fans; support details diminish quickly.
Use-size improvement should come from coherent rail/deck/wood masses and stable useful highlights before tiny decoration.
deadSpots: Original S/E outer rail obscures most warm supporting construction; any added detail must remain readable in those views without entering deck clearance or extending the registration.
Original N/W dark legs and abrupt flat wood lip are priorities for fuller warm form separation. These are source observations, not universal requirements for visible legs in every angle.
